introduction.text: The Basilica di Sant'Agnese fuori le mura is a titular church and minor basilica in Rome, built on a slope descending from Via Nomentana. It sits above the Catacombs of Saint Agnes, where the saint was originally buried, and contains a largely intact 7th‑century apse mosaic. The basilica is significant for its early Christian architecture, its connection to Saint Agnes, and its role as a titular church and parish.

history.description: Catacombs dating from the 2nd to the 5th centuries are accessible from the church.
A large basilica was built nearby in the 4th century, including a mausoleum for Constantina, later converted into Santa Costanza.
The present church was constructed by Pope Honorius I in the 7th century.
Pope Innocent VIII assigned the basilica to the Canons Regular of the Lateran in 1489.
Pope Clement XI made the basilica a parish church in 1708.
The Children of Mary sodality was founded at the basilica in 1864.
In 2026 a bust of Jesus Christ in the basilica was re‑attributed to Michelangelo.

design.description: Separate upper gallery for women (matronaeum) similar to that of San Lorenzo fuori le mura.
Long wide internal set of steps lined with inscriptions from the catacombs and other ancient buildings.
Floor level of the 7th‑century church is about two metres above the catacomb floor, with public street entrances at the level of the second‑floor gallery.

art.description: Apse mosaic from Honorius’s time depicting Saint Agnes in Byzantine empress costume, Pope Honorius, and another unidentified pope on a gold ground.
